scope: first original 7-Zip console/MSI frontend and inherited guided installer

questions.question: Is the next step clear?
questions.observations: Welcome explains choose/customize/review/restart; Review names the target and preserves Back; Finish makes Restart to Engine OS primary. Windows Apps names Install, Open, archive examples and Remove, with the console/GUI distinction visible.

questions.question: Is the task convenient?
questions.observations: The prepared VM includes a blank disk and original MSI. Normal installation, execution and removal need no terminal or network. Repeated sample tasks choose fresh outputs instead of requiring manual cleanup.

questions.question: Is it user friendly?
questions.observations: Install/remove require explicit review; documents are separate. Cancellation returns to a usable screen. Recovery is offered for interrupted products. The visible status does not claim unsupported Windows GUI integration.

questions.question: Is the graphical presentation coherent?
questions.observations: Native Inter text, shared mint/navy palette, rounded panels, consistent button geometry and spacing match the desktop. Images are real guest framebuffer/RFB captures, not a browser mockup.

questions.question: Is essential text readable?
questions.observations: Ordinary-resolution consent, cancellation, Welcome, Review and Finish have separated labels/actions and no observed essential-text clipping or overlap. The actual 3840x2160 Windows app frame uses native scaling and paged output rather than enlarging a bitmap font.

limitations: Agent scenario and visual review is not proof of usability for every inexperienced child or older adult
Firmware mode availability and manual appearance choices still apply
General Windows GUI and existing-ZIP update remain unqualified
